subject: RE: Post-call recap + Integration next steps (FinLytics) — 5xx on embeddings/reranker
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps — FinLytics integration

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the call this morning — good to hear more about how FinLytics will pipe search+recommendation requests into the Redwood API. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Objective: low-latency embeddings + reranker in front of your recommendation pipeline; 95th pct latency target of <150ms for rerank.
- SDK: you’ll use our JS SDK for client-side requests from the service, with a server-side proxy for API keys.
- Auth: customer-managed KMS for Private mode is a later phase; for PoC we recommended scoped API keys and per-route quotas.
- Structured output / tools: plan to use function calling to extract product IDs and a JSON reranker score.
- Risk: you mentioned intermittent 5xx when you replay the PoC load — we need repro steps and payloads to triage.

Next steps:
1) You to share a minimal failing request + sample response and logs (we discussed an attachment called api-request.json and repro-logs.txt).
2) I’ll loop in Dev to triage and propose timeout / retry tuning.
3) Rishi will propose batching / KV cache settings to hit your latency target.

If that matches your notes, can you send the sample request and one example 5xx response? I’ll open a support ticket and keep this thread for coordination.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.ai
From: Alex Johnson <alex@finlytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 10:18:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps — FinLytics integration

Thanks Camila — that recap is perfect. I’ve attached the small sample payload that consistently reproduces a 500 when we run it through our staging proxy (api-request.json).

Attached: api-request.json (minimal request), repro-logs.txt (nginx + service logs), screenshot-500.png (response body snapshot). The 5xx appears after ~1.2s and shows a server-side error referencing "Model backend: 500 Internal".

We do run retries client-side (3x, exponential backoff) but that only masks the symptom. Let me know if you want a curl snippet or a replay script — we can provide either.

-Alex
Senior Engineering Manager, FinLytics
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:05:14 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps — FinLytics integration

Thanks Alex — I have the attachments and took a first pass. A few immediate asks to help repro in our env:

1) Full request headers (including Authorization header redacted) and exact timestamp when the call was made.
2) The exact model variant you were hitting (model name + pinned version) — the error lines look like it came from a reranker variant with quantization enabled.
3) Whether you’re using streaming responses or the regular generate endpoint.

From a quick read of repro-logs.txt: we’re seeing an upstream 502 from a backend worker that timed out during KV cache deserialization under high concurrency. That can happen with large embeddings payloads + very short worker timeouts.

Immediate mitigation suggestions:
- Increase request timeout to 10s on the staging proxy for now.
- Disable client-side retries while we capture a single failing trace.
- Reduce concurrency in your replay (try 20 concurrent vs 100).

I’ll spin up a local repro and post findings by EOD. If anyone has a replay script, please drop it here.

--Dev
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finlytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 12:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps — FinLytics integration

Alex —
Appreciate the quick response and attachments. We’ll follow Dev’s mitigation steps so you can capture a clean single-trace failure. Rishi — can you prepare recommended batching/caching config for their request distribution? A draft we discussed: 64-token prefix cache TTL, KV deserialization batch size 8, and a per-route worker timeout bump to 10s.

Also looping Marissa for commercial context — if this turns into a larger triage (hotfix or on-call escalation), want to align on support scope for the PoC.

Camila
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps — FinLytics integration

Adding the config snippet I tested locally that improved stability:

- batching.max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
- batching.max_concurrent_batches: 4
- kv_cache.batch_deserialize_size: 8
- route.worker_request_timeout_ms: 10000
- client.retry_policy: disable (for debugging)

With these settings and a reduced replay concurrencies (20), I reproduced the 500 locally and fixed a race that surfaced in the deserializer (PR queued). I’ll push a patch to our staging runtime and cc this ticket once deployed.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finlytics.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps — FinLytics integration

Alex —
Thanks for the patience. We’ve deployed the staging patch and Rishi validated the KV deserializer fix. Could you re-run the replay with the reduced concurrency and the 10s timeout? If you hit any 5xxs, please forward the single-trace logs.

Commercial note: we’re happy to include hands-on triage support for this PoC through our standard PoC add-on. I’ll send a separate DocuSign for the add-on if you want Redwood engineers to run the replay/metrics capture with you.

Best,
Marissa Cole
